column7: AzureKeyVaultConnector.GetSecret had the identical defect as its AWS sibling (out.Value == nil, no empty-string guard) -- a response like {"value":""} returned success with an empty value; fixed by also requiring *out.Value != ""; the fuzzer's own oracle had the same pointer-only blind spot as the connector code, so it was strengthened too (now requires *ref.Value != ""), with a new {"value":""} seed added to lock in coverage; dedicated point test used as the proving test because FuzzAzureKVConnectorResponse is already the proving test for the unrelated connect-redirect-refusal-001 claim, and check-closures.sh's claim-name lookup does not disambiguate two claims sharing one (package, test) pair; see docs/findings/2026-09-20-FINDING-awssm-empty-secret-response.md
